- **Act-wide organization / references**
  - Sec. 1: Organizes Act into Divisions A–T; names each division, including Israel, Ukraine, Indo-Pacific supplemental appropriations; 21st Century Peace through Strength Act; FEND Off Fentanyl Act; REPO for Ukrainians Act; and other sanctions/data/application-related divisions.
  - Sec. 2: Unless expressly provided otherwise, “this Act” within any division refers only to that division.

- **Division A — Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2024**
  - Appropriates FY2024 supplemental amounts; generally emergency-designated under Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act §251(b)(2)(A)(i), available only if President designates.
  - DOD: $4,400,000,000 O&M Defense-Wide through 9/30/2025 for Israel response; transfer to O&M/procurement/revolving funds for replacement/repair/reimbursement of defense articles/services/training to Israel or supporting countries; 15-day defense committee notice; retransfer permitted.
  - DOD procurement: $801,400,000 Army ammunition through 9/30/2026; $5,200,000,000 Defense-Wide through 9/30/2026, including $4,000,000,000 Iron Dome/David’s Sling and $1,200,000,000 Iron Beam, via exchange of letters, additional to U.S.-Israel Iron Dome Procurement Agreement; $198,600,000 Defense Production Act Purchases until expended under 50 U.S.C. 4518, 4531–4533.
  - DOD general: $2,440,000,000 through 9/30/2024 for transfer to personnel/O&M/procurement/RDT&E/Defense Working Capital Funds for U.S. operations, force protection, deterrence, combat expenditure replacement in CENTCOM; obligation barred until 30 days after execution plan; 15-day transfer notice.
  - DHS/FEMA: $10,000,000 Operations and Support through 9/30/2027 for nonprofit security grant administration; $390,000,000 Federal Assistance for Nonprofit Security Grant Program under Homeland Security Act §2009, 6 U.S.C. 609a ($160,000,000 through 9/30/2025; $230,000,000 through 9/30/2026); FEMA may expedite/flex use; States may use up to 2% for outreach/technical assistance, prioritizing rural/underserved/underrepresented nonprofits.
  - State/USAID/humanitarian/security: $150,000,000 Diplomatic Programs through 9/30/2025, including $100,000,000 WSP until expended; $4,000,000 State OIG through 9/30/2025; $50,000,000 Emergencies until expended; $3,000,000 USAID OIG through 9/30/2025; $5,655,000,000 International Disaster Assistance until expended; $3,495,000,000 Migration and Refugee Assistance until expended; $75,000,000 INCLE through 9/30/2025 for Middle East after consultation; $10,000,000 Peacekeeping through 9/30/2025 including MFO Sinai; $3,500,000,000 FMF through 9/30/2025 for Israel, up to $769,300,000 for procurement in Israel unless exceeded by U.S.-Israel agreement after Appropriations consultation; Israel notifications waivable by Secretary of State; up to $5,000,000 admin.
  - State general: FY2024 transfer up to $250,000,000 from Consular and Border Security Programs to Diplomatic Programs/WSP/Emergencies after consultation/notification. FY2024 Foreign Assistance Act drawdown caps applied as: §506(a)(1), 22 U.S.C. 2318(a)(1), $7,800,000,000; §506(a)(2)(B), $400,000,000 and clause (i) $150,000,000; §552(c)(2), 22 U.S.C. 2348a(c)(2), $50,000,000.
  - Amends Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2005 §12001: Israel reserve stock transfers cover DOD inventory defense articles located in Israel stockpile; reimbursement amount determined by Secretary of Defense; advance notice may be as practicable as President determines in extraordinary national security circumstances. FY2024 Foreign Assistance Act §514(b), 22 U.S.C. 2321h(b), inapplicable to Israel stockpiles

1.notes:
- **Div. E, Title I (FEND Off Fentanyl sanctions), §§3101–3105 (21 U.S.C. 2351–2355):**
  - §3101: Finds international trafficking of fentanyl, fentanyl precursors, or related opioids is an unusual and extraordinary threat and national emergency; states U.S. policy to apply economic/financial sanctions to such traffickers.
  - §3102: Authorizes President to use IEEPA §§203, 205 (50 U.S.C. 1702, 1704). Requires report to appropriate committees within **180 days** of enactment and annually on executive actions under subtitle and fentanyl/illicit-drug emergencies; unclassified, classified annex allowed for outside information, licenses, enforcement cases, mitigation procedures.
  - §3103: Requires sanctions on foreign persons determined knowingly involved in significant fentanyl/precursor/related-opioid trafficking or significant related transnational criminal organization activity. Sanctions: IEEPA blocking/prohibitions on property/interests in U.S. jurisdiction or U.S.-person control. Report within **180 days** and annually on identified persons.
  - §3104: Applies IEEPA §206(b),(c) penalties (50 U.S.C. 1705) to violations/attempts/conspiracies/causing violations. President may waive sanctions on national-security-interest determination. Exceptions: title V National Security Act/intelligence activities; UN Headquarters Agreement/other international obligations or U.S. law enforcement admission/parole; no sanctions for agricultural commodities, food, medicine, medical devices, humanitarian assistance.
  - §3105: Covered forfeited property must be deposited into Treasury Forfeiture Fund (31 U.S.C. 9705) or DOJ Assets Forfeiture Fund (28 U.S.C. 524(c)); report within **180 days** and every **180 days** on deposits. Covered property: forfeited under 18 U.S.C. ch. 46 or §1963 and belonged to/possessed by person affiliated/connected to TCO sanctioned under this subtitle, Fentanyl Sanctions Act (21 U.S.C. 2301 et seq.), or E.O. 14059. Does not affect blocked terrorist-party assets under Terrorism Risk Insurance Act §201(a).

- **Div. E, Subtitle B / Title II / Title III:**
  - §3111: Amends IEEPA §206 (50 U.S.C. 1705) and Trading with the Enemy Act §16 (50 U.S.C. 4315) to add **10-year** limitations for civil enforcement and criminal indictment/information; civil commencement includes pre-penalty notice or finding of violation.
  - §§3112–3114: Within **180 days**, require classified OFAC staffing report/briefing; classified Treasury/interagency report/briefing on drug routes, vessel/cargo mislabeling, precursor customer tracking; classified report/briefing on PRC actions re fentanyl supply-chain persons.
  - §3201: Amends Fentanyl Sanctions Act subtitle A by adding §7213A (21 U.S.C. 2313a): Treasury may designate foreign financial institutions, transaction classes, or account types as primary money laundering concern for illicit opioid trafficking and impose NDAA FY2021 §9714(a)(1) special measures or prohibit/condition fund transmittals; classified information may be submitted ex parte/in camera; applies §9714(c) disclosure exemptions, §9714(d) penalties, §9714(e) injunction authority. Clerical amendment to NDAA FY2020 table.
  - §3202 (21 U.S.C. 2361): FinCEN Director must issue SAR filing guidance/instructions within **180 days** for suspected TCO fentanyl trafficking under 31 C.F.R. 1010.320; prioritize research into reports tied to fentanyl/synthetic opioids or suspected TCO financing.
  - §3203: First post-enactment illicit-finance national strategy update must include report on trade-based money laundering originating in Mexico or PRC and involving Burma; defines strategy by CAATSA §261 as amended by NDAA FY2022 §6506.
  - §3301 (21 U.S.C. 2371): Blocking authority/requirements under division do not include sanctions on importation of goods; “good” excludes technical data.

- **Div. F (REPO for Ukrainians Act):**
  - §1 short title/table; §2 definitions include Russian aggressor state, sovereign assets, U.S./financial institutions, “seize.” Findings cite approx. **$300,000,000,000** immobilized worldwide, **$4,000,000,000–$5,000,000,000** in U.S. jurisdiction, approx. **$190,000,000,000** in Belgium.
  - §§103–105: Prohibits release/mobilization of Treasury-blocked/effectively immobilized Russian sovereign assets before §104(j) date absent certification hostilities ceased and compensation/mechanism conditions met; **30-day** advance notice and joint-resolution disapproval.

- **Amounts:** no dollar amounts are appropriated or authorized in these divisions.

- **Division L—Mahsa Amini Human Rights and Security**
  - **Iran Supreme Leader/President sanctions determinations (22 U.S.C. 8501 note):** Within **90 days** of enactment and annually, President must determine whether covered Iranian officials/entities/persons meet criteria under listed sanctions authorities; impose sanctions under **CISADA §105(c), 22 U.S.C. 8514(c)** and **State/Foreign Operations Appropriations Act, 2021 §7031(c)** where applicable; pursue sanctions under **E.O. 13553, 13224, 13818, 13876** where applicable.
  - Report to specified committees: unclassified, classified annex if needed; list covered persons, applicable authorities, sanctions imposed/to be imposed within **30 days**, and waiver/nonapplication authority plus justification.
  - Covered persons: Supreme Leader/office; President/office/cabinet; Supreme Leader-overseen entities complicit in financing/resourcing human rights abuses or terrorism; officials of entities owned/controlled by Supreme Leader/office; appointees, material supporters, owned/controlled actors, board members/senior executives of blocked persons.
  - Congressional request mechanism: within **60 days** of bipartisan committee leadership request, President determines whether person meets subsection (d)(5) criteria and reports sanctions decision.
  - Severability: unconstitutional provision/application does not affect remainder.

- **Division M—Hamas and Other Palestinian Terrorist Groups International Financing Prevention Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 note)**
  - Policy: prevent Hamas, PIJ, Al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigade, Lion’s Den, affiliates/successors from accessing support networks and using goods to smuggle weapons/materials.
  - Foreign-person sanctions: within **180 days**, President must block property under **IEEPA, 50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.**, for knowing significant support for terrorism or significant transactions with senior members of listed groups or FTOs supporting them. IEEPA §206 penalties apply.
  - Regulations/guidance due **60 days**. Waiver: case-by-case, max **180 days**, **15-day** prior congressional justification, vital national security.
  - Humanitarian carveout for agricultural commodities, food, medicine, medical devices, humanitarian assistance/purposes and related transactions.
  - Foreign-state measures: within **180 days**, impose at least **1-year** U.S. assistance suspension, IFI opposition/vote against loans/assistance for **1 year**, and **1-year** export prohibition for USML/Commerce Control List items if state supports terrorism/listed groups or significant transactions materially contributing to their terrorist activities. SOFA/basing, intelligence, humanitarian exemptions.
  - Reports due **90 days** and every **180 days** on assets/fundraising/financing/money laundering and state support/locations/equipment transfers.
  - Terminates after **7 years** or **30 days** after presidential certification that listed designation/sanctions/Palestinian Anti-Terrorism Act criteria conditions are met.

- **Division N—No Technology for Terror Act (50 U.S.C. 4811 note)**
  - Starting **90 days** after enactment, applies Export Administration Regulations under **Export Control Reform Act of 2018, 50 U.S.C. 4801 et seq.**, to specified foreign-direct products exported/reexported/in-country transferred to Iran or involving Government of Iran.
  - License required for covered foreign-produced items meeting product/destination scopes; exceptions for EAR99/non-CCL food, medicine, medical devices and certain communications services/software/hardware under general license, excluding Government of Iran-owned/controlled end users.
  - Commerce Secretary may waive in U.S. national interest with report to committees. Sunset after **7 years**.
